correctness.rationale: The definition removes all 27 geometric lines, including nonrational ones. The classical line equations and Frobenius action give two surface cardinalities and a nonsplit-descent lemma; the Eisenstein norm certificates exhaust 351 pairs and 2,925 triples, ruling out unaccounted specializations outside p=2,3. In characteristic two, exact F4 Hermitian incidence has 45 triple points. Hence union cardinalities 27q−90, 27q−63, 3q, 3q+1, respectively, establish all four exact formulas. The set of zeros follows by checking permissible prime powers. Applying formulas over every extension and the logarithmic zeta identity establishes all four zeta functions. Verifier was executed and replayed from the actual current public package, with identical outputs. The exhaustive finite computations support the universal algebraic certificate rather than substitute for it.

value.rationale: Removing all geometric exceptional curves is a canonical open subset used to isolate points not lying on lines on a smooth cubic surface. Determining whether such points exist is a natural arithmetic existence question; the exact answer has five exceptional finite fields and requires separate treatment of split/nonsplit cube roots and the genuine characteristic-two Hermitian collision. Complete point counts over all extensions yield rational zeta functions, a reusable geometric invariant. These outcomes are not just a type correction or an arbitrary numerical slice; the strongest phenomenon is that entire rational surfaces can have every rational point trapped on their exceptional curves.
